atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported 172,556 children, 217,958 supporters, $391.9 million raised, and 327 projects in 40 countries in its 2024 snapshot.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported that 84% of total operating expenses were used for field programs and advocacy work during 2024.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported making a material difference in the lives of over 7.5 million people across 40 countries during 2024.
qualifications: Statement by the Board Chair in the 2024 annual report.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported reaching over 7.5 million people in 40 countries during 2024 with generous Australians.
qualifications: Statement by the Chief Executive Officer in the 2024 annual report.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia described itself as a Christian charity dedicated to empowering everyday Australians to help vulnerable children around the world live life to the fullest.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported that its work includes transformational development, emergency relief, promoting justice, and engaging Australians to support vulnerable children.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported serving all people regardless of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender, and collaborating with people of all faiths and with people who share its values.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported being part of the global World Vision Partnership, which has more than 34,000 staff in nearly 100 countries.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported that its 327 projects in 40 countries reached 7,554,870 people.
qualifications: Organisation self-report; page presents this as a project/program reach figure.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported that Australian sponsors and donors provide funds for World Vision field offices to run relief and development projects, with technical support from the World Vision Australia team.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia reported working directly with First Nations communities in Australia to run activities and ensure those communities drive their own development.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia stated that it is committed to working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and to maintaining and strengthening respectful partnerships and relationships with Australian First Nations peoples.
qualifications: Statement in the organisation's acknowledgment of country.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: In FY24, World Vision Australia worked with partners in 40 countries across 327 projects, and everyday Australians reached 7.5 million people through supporting its work.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: In FY24, World Vision Australia had 92 Area Programs undertaking 226 projects across 21 countries and opened 11 new Area Programs.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: In FY24, 319,706 people participated in World Vision Australia's Australian NGO Cooperation Program across 32 projects in 20 countries.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia delivers humanitarian response and international community development programming across five key sectors: livelihoods; health and nutrition; education; water, sanitation and hygiene; and child protection.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: In FY24, World Vision Australia's sector reach included 146 livelihoods projects in 26 countries reaching over 2,353,454 people; 58 health and nutrition projects in 25 countries reaching over 1,385,108 people; 56 education projects in 24 countries reaching over 625,797 people; 33 water and sanitation projects in 14 countries reaching over 724,550 people; and 32 child protection projects in 14 countries reaching over 655,540 people.
qualifications: Sector reach figures are calculated separately from total reach figures because a participant could be engaged in multiple projects at the same time.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia undertakes scheduled evaluations and reviews of all its programs and projects to assess their impact on participants, with particular focus on vulnerable or excluded people, including people with disability, women and children.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: In 2024, World Vision Australia conducted 12 evaluations and reviews, including seven evaluations and five mid-term reviews.
qualifications: Most of these projects were supported by the Australian Government through the Australian NGO Cooperation Program.

unsupported_exact_date_diagnostics.proposition: In 2024, World Vision Australia conducted 12 evaluations and reviews, including seven evaluations and five mid-term reviews.

OUR COMMITMENT We are committed to demonstrating a credible account of change
through our programs.
TO ACCOUNTABILITY We undertake scheduled evaluations and reviews of all our
programs and projects to assess their impact on the lives of
participants. We focus especially on those who are the most
vulnerable or excluded, including people with disability, women
and children. Insights and lessons learned from these assessments
are used to improve the quality and effectiveness of current and
new projects and programs.
In 2024, we conducted 12 evaluations and reviews, including
seven evaluations and five mid-term reviews. Most of these
projects are supported by the Australian Government through the
Australian NGO Cooperation Program (ANCP). Our ANCP projects
are complex and often bring several sectors of community
development together. This year, substantial work took place
across five programs: climate action and natural resource
management; economic empowerment; food security, health
and nutrition; water, sanitation and hygiene; and child protection,
education and rights.

atoms.subject: World Vision Australia
atoms.proposition: World Vision Australia developed an evidence-building strategy in 2020 aimed at improving how it collects, aggregates and uses evidence of impact.

unsupported_exact_date_diagnostics.proposition: World Vision Australia developed an evidence-building strategy in 2020 aimed at improving how it collects, aggregates and uses evidence of impact.

THE WAY In 2020, we developed an evidence-building strategy aimed at improving the way we collect,
aggregate and utilise evidence of impact. This has enabled us to generate credible evidence of
our impact and effectiveness at the portfolio level. We publicly disseminate results from a series
WE MEASURE
of meta-reviews, meta-learning and case studies. For wider dissemination of our impact at scale,
we are exploring the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to translate our findings into succinct impact
statements and stories across our portfolio of projects.
IMPACT
Our evidence building and research agenda is focused on three priority evidence pillars:
climate action and regenerative environment; economic empowerment; and food security,
health and nutrition; as well as cross-cutting themes on gender equality, disability and social
inclusion.
It is implemented through our evidence building framework, involving the use of a standardised
monitoring and evaluation approach. This is to ensure a minimum level of quality assurance and
consistency in selecting a set of priority indicators for each evidence pillar. We also use a set of
guidance notes, tools and ongoing training to build capacity and support national project teams
in countries where we operate.
In 2024, we concluded three meta-reviews: Partnerships for Scaling Farmer Managed Natural
Regeneration (FMNR), FMNR Evidence Gap Map, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture.
